fact: FAO says the EOSTAT-Zimbabwe project, launched in 2023 with African Development Bank funding and implemented with the Ministry of Lands, Agriculture, Fisheries, Water and Rural Development, ZIMSTAT, ZINGSA and others, is rolling out an Earth-observation crop monitoring system and crop type and yield data practices.

Digital Earth Africa and SASSCAL agreed to build the AgriWatch dashboard on DE Africa Earth-observation products for crop-cycle, rangeland and rainfall monitoring, with AgriWatch covering this country among the six SASSCAL states.

FAO says EOSTAT Phase II, launched with the Ministry of Lands, Agriculture, Fisheries, Water and Rural Development, will make satellite crop type mapping routine and expand Earth-observation tools for drought and flood early warning, after a first phase that produced a 2023 winter wheat map, a 2023/24 summer crop type map and pilot drought and flood tools.

FAO says its EOSTAT system helps Zimbabwe generate crop and yield estimates from satellite data with over 80 percent accuracy and tracks droughts and floods in real time, and a Ministry early warning specialist describes it as modernising agricultural monitoring.
